transcript.text:
Thank you all three for your critical inputs. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I finalize the authorization:

1. Ravi (Lab Quality): The spent coolant shows 2.4% chlorinated solvent, which exceeds the 1.0% threshold in our waste matrix. These drums must be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment, not ordinary coolant recycling.

2. Megan (Waste Logistics): The disposal contractor's tanker permit limits each load to 8 drums maximum, so we need two shipments — one of 8 drums and one of 6 drums. This split-shipment condition needs to be entered in the transport booking system.

3. Tomas (Warehouse Supervision): 4 of the 14 drums have active seepage and require UN-rated overpacks before any movement. The other 10 drums are fine on their existing spill pallets.

Based on this review, I'm prepared to authorize the following: route all 14 drums to hazardous-liquid treatment, split across two shipments (8 and 6), with the 4 seeping drums placed in UN-rated overpacks. I'll also need commitments to get the lab results attached to the waste authorization, the permit condition entered in the transport booking system, and the warehouse inspection findings formally updated in the waste file. Are there any objections before I issue the formal authorization?
